successors.name: Mali Empire
successors.text: 'Around 1286, the Mali Empire conquered Takrur and put it under a military dictatorship ruled by farba (governors)'

capitals.name: Takrur (seat uncertain; Tumbere Jiinge in the Gorgol valley)

ledger.x: c. 1040: Takrur, the Senegal River kingdom that had adopted Sharia under War Jabi in 1035, passes to his son Lebi. The state is older than the map shows: infobox 'Established: 9th century', 'founded as early as 100 CE' (Clark), and a Soninke clan under Mamadu Sumaare 'conquered Takrur in the 9th or 10th century'; no…

c. 1285: Mali conquers Takrur. 'Around 1286, the Mali Empire conquered Takrur and put it under a military dictatorship ruled by farba (governors)'; infobox 'Conquered and vassalized by Mali Empire: c. 1285'. The year follows the infobox.
c. 1285: the last independent Takrur ends under Mali's farba governors. The land later passed to Jolof and in 1513/1521 to Koli Tenguella's Denianke.

wars.name: War Jabi's holy war against Silla
wars.outcome: No territorial result is recorded: 'During his reign he launched a Holy War against the King of Silla'.

wars.name: Mali conquest of Takrur
wars.outcome: Takrur became a Mali province under farba governors.

certainty.note: A river kingdom with fluid frontiers; the pages give no boundary.
